property_summary: For any call that does not revert, the return value must be true; the mutant returns false on success, violating this invariant.

For any input, the reference contract always requires at least one recipient to execute transfers; the buggy version allows an empty _tos array and then proceeds with no calls, causing a difference in observable behavior when checking the success return value.
The reference always returns true from transfer, while the buggy mutant returns the default false, so after any valid call the return value differs.

The reference contract guarantees that the entire transfer call reverts if any internal transferFrom call fails, while the buggy version incorrectly succeeds, returning true even when some calls failed.

For any admissible input, the correct contract successfully makes external calls using the 'transferFrom' selector, while the buggy version uses the 'transfer' selector which will fail when the external contract does not implement that function, causing the entire transaction to revert.

For any call to transfer with a helper contract that implements transferFrom(address,address,uint256) but not transfer(address,uint256), the reference C's call succeeds while the mutant's call reverts because it uses the wrong selector.
